# chalk_sandbox (Resource)

Manages a Chalk sandbox — an ephemeral container running in the environment's cluster, addressable for command execution via `chalk sandbox exec`.

Only `desired_state` can be updated in place; every other argument forces replacement.

A sandbox has **no outbound network access by default**: without a `network_policy` even DNS resolution fails. Grant egress explicitly via `network_policy.allowed_routes`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Chalk sandbox: an ephemeral container in the environment's cluster that you
# can exec into with `chalk sandbox exec <id> -- <command>`.
#
# A sandbox has no outbound network access by default — without a network_policy
# even DNS resolution fails — so egress is granted explicitly below.

resource "chalk_sandbox" "workstation" {
  environment_id = "tmnmc9beyujew"
  name           = "debian-workstation"
  image          = "debian:bookworm"
  # Set desired_state to opt into lifecycle management. When omitted, Terraform
  # leaves out-of-band suspend and resume changes alone.
  desired_state = "suspended"
  # Coder pattern: data.coder_workspace.me.start_count == 1 ? "running" : "suspended"

  entrypoint = ["/bin/bash", "-c", "sleep infinity"]

  env = {
    WORKSPACE = "demo"
  }

  resource_limits = {
    cpu    = "2"
    memory = "4Gi"
  }

  volumes = [{
    name       = "home"
    mount_path = "/home/dev"
    type       = "empty_dir"
    size_limit = "20Gi"
  }]

  network_policy = {
    # Full egress. Narrow this to the CIDRs the workload actually needs.
    allowed_routes = [{
      route = "0.0.0.0/0"
    }]

    # The cloud metadata endpoint is never something a sandbox should reach.
    denied_routes = ["169.254.169.254/32"]
  }
}

# GCP workload identity federation without a Google key in the sandbox. The
# sandbox runs as its own workload principal; Chalk mints an OIDC token for the
# workload identity provider's audience, writes it to a file, points
# GCP_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE at that file, and rotates it before expiry. Inside the
# sandbox, an `external_account` credential config whose
# credential_source.file is that path lets Google client libraries exchange it.
resource "chalk_sandbox" "gcp_wif" {
  environment_id = "tmnmc9beyujew"
  image          = "google/cloud-sdk:slim"

  chalk_workload_identity = {
    mode = "workload_principal"
    oidc_token_files = [{
      audience = "//iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER"
      env_var  = "GCP_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE"
    }]
  }

  # The token exchange needs egress to sts.googleapis.com and the Google APIs.
  network_policy = {
    allowed_routes = [{ route = "0.0.0.0/0" }]
    denied_routes  = ["169.254.169.254/32"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) The environment ID that this sandbox runs in.
- `image` (String) Pre-built container image to run, e.g. `debian:bookworm`.

### Optional

- `chalk_workload_identity` (Attributes) Chalk-managed identity for the sandbox, fixed at create. With `mode = "workload_principal"` the sandbox runs as its own workload principal and can declare `oidc_token_files`: the platform mints an OIDC token per audience, writes it to a file, sets `env_var` to that file's path, and rotates it before expiry. Use this for cloud workload identity federation (e.g. GCP) without long-lived keys in the sandbox. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chalk_workload_identity))
- `desired_state` (String) Desired lifecycle state: `running` or `suspended`. When set, changing this value suspends or restores the sandbox in place and out-of-band state changes are corrected on the next apply. When omitted, Terraform does not manage whether the sandbox is running or suspended.
- `entrypoint` (List of String) Overrides the image's entrypoint. When unset, the image's own entrypoint is used. `exec` into the sandbox keeps working either way — it does not go through the entrypoint process.
- `env` (Map of String, Sensitive) Environment variables to inject into the sandbox.
- `name` (String) Optional human-readable name for the sandbox. The server generates one when omitted.
- `network_policy` (Attributes) Outbound network policy. **Without this, the sandbox cannot reach anything — not even DNS.** Grant full egress with a single `allowed_routes` entry for `0.0.0.0/0`. The server rejects network policies when `runtime` is `kube`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_policy))
- `resource_limits` (Attributes) CPU and memory limits for the sandbox container. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_limits))
- `restart_policy` (String) Whether to recreate the sandbox after its backing instance terminates: `RESTART_POLICY_NEVER` (default) or `RESTART_POLICY_ALWAYS`.
- `runtime` (String) Runtime backend for the sandbox container. When unset, the provider sends no runtime and the server default (host compute) is used. `chalk_node` or `local` select host compute; `kube` selects Kubernetes. The server rejects `kube` when `network_policy` is set.
- `volumes` (Attributes List) Volumes to mount into the sandbox. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volumes))
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Whether to block until the sandbox reports a ready state before completing the apply. Defaults to `true`; set to `false` to return as soon as the create call is accepted.

### Read-Only

- `build_id` (String, Deprecated) Deprecated: always null because the v2 sandbox API does not return build IDs.
- `created_at` (String) When the sandbox was created.
- `id` (String) The sandbox id.
- `state` (String) Current sandbox state, e.g. `running`, `pending`, or `suspended`.
- `status_message` (String) Additional detail about the current state.

<a id="nestedatt--chalk_workload_identity"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chalk_workload_identity`

Required:

- `mode` (String) Identity mode: `workload_principal` (the sandbox is its own principal) or `creator_identity` (the sandbox acts as its creator).

Optional:

- `oidc_token_files` (Attributes List) OIDC token files the platform materializes and keeps fresh, at most 8. Requires `mode = "workload_principal"` and host compute (the server rejects them with `runtime = "kube"`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chalk_workload_identity--oidc_token_files))

<a id="nestedatt--chalk_workload_identity--oidc_token_files"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chalk_workload_identity.oidc_token_files`

Required:

- `audience` (String) Audience claim of the token, e.g. a GCP workload identity provider `//iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER`.
- `env_var` (String) Environment variable that receives the absolute path of the token file.



<a id="nestedatt--network_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_policy`

Optional:

- `allowed_routes` (Attributes List) Allowlist of destination CIDRs and the ports permitted on each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_policy--allowed_routes))
- `denied_routes` (List of String) Denylist of destination CIDRs. Takes precedence over `allowed_routes`.

<a id="nestedatt--network_policy--allowed_routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_policy.allowed_routes`

Required:

- `route` (String) Destination CIDR, e.g. `10.0.0.0/8`.

Optional:

- `port_ranges` (Attributes List) Destination ports allowed for this route. Omit to allow all ports. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_policy--allowed_routes--port_ranges))

<a id="nestedatt--network_policy--allowed_routes--port_ranges"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_policy.allowed_routes.port_ranges`

Required:

- `end_port` (Number) Inclusive end port, at least `start_port`.
- `start_port` (Number) Inclusive start port.




<a id="nestedatt--resource_limits"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_limits`

Optional:

- `cpu` (String) CPU limit, e.g. `2` or `500m`.
- `memory` (String) Memory limit, e.g. `4Gi` or `512Mi`.


<a id="nestedatt--volumes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volumes`

Required:

- `mount_path` (String) Path inside the sandbox to mount the volume at.
- `name` (String) Name of the volume.
- `type` (String) Volume type: `empty_dir`, `shared_memory`, `chalkfs`, or `versioned_chalkfs`.

Optional:

- `size_limit` (String) Size limit for the volume, e.g. `2Gi`. Optional for `empty_dir`.
- `version_id` (Number) Pins a `versioned_chalkfs` mount to an immutable committed snapshot.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Sandboxes are imported as environment_id/sandbox_id.
terraform import chalk_sandbox.workstation tmnmc9beyujew/ad287d61-6de5-4fe0-b0bf-0c24b2cd22a5
```
